transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Friday, November 20. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. Rajasthan IAS officer's kin bought 64 villas in Jaipur, 24 of them at 11L each: ACB. Rajasthan high court has denied senior IAS officer Shikhar Agrawal interim protection from a thorough ACB investigation. This inquiry concerns the alleged purchase of villas from Goyal Fashions Pvt Ltd. Agrawal claimed wrongful implications but the court has encouraged him to pursue anticipatory bail. The ACB has already registered an FIR against Agrawal and two directors of Goyal Fashions. US may reverse its immigration curbs: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu. Sridhar Vembu, founder of Zoho, believes changes in US immigration policy may occur due to recent political shifts. He argues that these changes could positively impact both legal and illegal immigration. Vembu links immigration to housing demand, stating that immigrants significantly contribute to the housing market. He notes that tighter immigration rules have temporarily reduced this demand, which could return if policies change. Phillips scripts history, becomes 1st batter to achieve rare feat against India. Phillips completed his century in the first innings of the ongoing Test, having already scored hundreds against India in ODIs and T20Is earlier this year. He made 106 in the ODI at Indore on January 18 before scoring 107 off 49 balls in the T20I at Auckland on October 30. Isolated Awá tribe emerges from Amazon amid illegal invasion threat. Recently, the elusive Awá tribe, famed for their isolation, reached out to a neighboring settlement in the Arariboia Indigenous territory. In search of food and assistance, their visit exposed the severe impacts of illegal land encroachments. Local villagers documented the meeting, bringing attention to the perils that Indigenous people face. Advocacy groups are demanding stronger safeguards and acknowledgment of the rights of uncontacted tribes to preserve their way of life. 50/4 and a lot of heat: How Akash Deep sparked India's turnaround on day 2. India endured a frustrating morning as Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips extended their sixth-wicket partnership to 216, but Akash Deep's dismissal of Phillips sparked a turnaround. India struck quickly thereafter, taking New Zealand's last four wickets for just 30 runs to bowl them out for 368. The visitors' post 'Compromised PM can never sit here': Rahul's dig at Modi with 'G3' pic from China summit. //t.co/EpGZVnJPYq Georgia has added 327 acres beside the Chattahoochee River to McIntosh Reserve. The recent addition of 327 acres has significantly expanded the footprint of McIntosh Reserve in Carroll County, Georgia. This effort not only aims to safeguard the scenic Chattahoochee River corridor but also enhances public access to green spaces for locals. An envisioned eight-mile trail connecting McIntosh Reserve to Moore's Bridge Park promotes outdoor activities. Karnataka farmer's son lifts 760kg for Commonwealth silver, struggles for funds. At the Commonwealth Powerlifting Championships in Winnipeg, Canada, Sachin Salunke clinched a silver medal, lifting an impressive 760 kg, and narrowly missing gold by a mere 10 kg. Despite his remarkable success, Sachin grapples with financial challenges stemming from his family's agricultural roots. He invests around rupees 30,000 monthly to maintain training and competition participation. Bengali or English? Bangladesh questions signature on Hasina's passport letter. Bangladesh has questioned the authenticity of a fresh letter reportedly sent by London-based Matrix Chambers to the Acting High Commissioner of Bangladesh in New Delhi concerning former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's passport and National Identity Card (NID). America's largest bank JPMorgan Chase says its vendors hacked: Read full statement. JPMorgan Chase revealed that hackers stole sensitive personal data of around 16,000 wealthy clients on November 19. The breach occurred via compromised third-party vendors rather than directly from the bank's internal systems. Clients associated with the bank's exclusive Reserve program were affected, prompting the bank to offer support for those impacted. This announcement followed a recent technical failure causing online banking disruptions for multiple institutions. Homeless at 11, Texas man later helps deliver 29,000 Thanksgiving meals. Rob Adams, a childhood homelessness survivor, started Thanksgiving Heroes to assist struggling families. Since its launch, the charity has provided more than 29,000 meals in nine U.S. cities. Through collaborations and dedicated volunteers, the organization alleviates the financial strain of Thanksgiving for families.

A bizarre whale that lived roughly 6 million years ago had a face so dramatically crooked that scientists believe it may have been the most asymmetrical of any mammal. Discovered in Peru, the extinct pygmy sperm whale Scaphokogia huachafo had an enormous downward-curving snout and a skull so distorted that researchers initially thought it had been damaged after death. Instead, its strange anatomy appears to have been an extraordinary evolutionary adaptation for hunting along the seafloor. The Asus ExpertBook P5 combines Intel Core Ultra 7 performance, a lightweight aluminium design, a sharp 2.5K display and AI-powered productivity features to deliver a premium business laptop experience. In an announcement on Thursday, the FCC argues the rule will help combat an "influx of contraband cellphones" used to carry out crimes from prison. Scientists have discovered a strange bacterium hiding beneath the skin of deep-sea creatures known as sea pigs, revealing an unexpected biological partnership. The microbe has an unusually tiny genome, yet more than a quarter of its DNA is devoted to making surface proteins, some of them exceptionally large. Researchers suspect it depends heavily on its host for survival, but what the sea pigs gain in return remains a mystery.
